ui.lede: The Elder Futhark has 24 runes. Ask a question, choose a spread and draw the runes. Each rune is shown with what we know historically about its name, and with a modern interpretation.
ui.questionPlaceholder: Your question, e.g. “What should I take with me into winter?”
ui.revealHint: Tap the stones to turn them over, or choose “Reveal all”.
ui.faceDownNote: {n} stone(s) landed blank side up and are not read.
ui.ringsLegend: Inner ring: the core of the matter · middle: what influences it · outer: background
ui.symNote: This rune looks the same both ways and therefore has no reversed interpretation.
ui.aiNote: The AI features below only work when the page is opened in Claude.
ui.aiDesc: AI reads the runes together based on your question: main theme, rune by rune, how they connect, and advice.
ui.photoDesc: Upload a photo of your rune stones, taken straight from above. We recognise the runes, you check the list, and then you get the interpretation.
ui.spreadOnPhoto: Which spread is in the photo
ui.found: Found {n} runes. Check the list before interpreting.
ui.noneFound: Found no runes in the image. Try a sharper photo taken straight from above.
ui.refDesc: The futhark is traditionally divided into three aettir of eight runes. Choose a rune to see its name, what it means, and the modern interpretation.
ui.footer: Rune reading on this site is culture, reflection and entertainment. It is not medical, legal or financial advice, and no results are guaranteed. The runes are drawn at random. The interpretations are modern: we have no reliable sources that runes were used for divination in the Viking Age. The AI interpretation is produced by artificial intelligence, not by a human.
ui.sourcesNote: Historical information: reconstructed Proto-Germanic names and the Old Norse and Old English rune poems (Store norske leksikon, Wikipedia with sources). Three runes (ᛉ, ᛊ, ᛟ) have been misused in Nazi and extremist symbolism; here they are used only in their original meaning.

ui.heroStoneHint: The same rune for everyone today. Tap to read about it.
ui.clothCaption: The Roman historian Tacitus described around the year 98 how Germanic peoples threw marked pieces of wood onto a white cloth to seek answers. Whether the marks were runes, no one knows.
ui.nameDesc: Write a name or a word and we will write it in the Elder Futhark.
ui.nameEmpty: Write something above to see it in runes.
ui.nameNote: This is a modern phonetic spelling. There was no fixed rule for writing present-day names in the Elder Futhark, and letters such as c, q, x and y have no rune of their own.
ui.booksDesc: Norwegian black books (svartebøker) are handwritten books of charms and advice from about 1480 to 1850. Most deal with protection and healing. This section is a work in progress.
ui.booksNote: Harmful magic, coercion and curses are mentioned only as history, never as a recipe.

en.label: Rune of the day
en.desc: One rune as the theme for the day.

tre.label: The Norns (3)
tre.desc: Three runes named after the Norns in the Völuspá: Urd, Verdandi and Skuld. The spread itself is a modern custom.

ni.label: Cast of nine runes
ni.desc: Nine runes are cast onto the cloth. Only runes with the symbol facing up are read, and the closer to the centre, the more important. This is a modern practice.

runes.name: Fehu
runes.hist: The Old Norse rune poem uses the name fé, the Old English feoh.
runes.up: Prosperity, assets you have worked for, something that can be shared.
runes.rev: Loss, unrest around money, assets slipping away.

runes.name: Uruz
runes.hist: The Old English rune poem says aurochs, the Icelandic one says rain or bad weather.
runes.up: Raw strength, health, endurance.

runes.name: Thurisaz
runes.hist: The Old Norse poems say þurs (giant), the Old English þorn (thorn).
runes.up: An opposition that must be faced, protection, a threshold.
runes.rev: Rash action, a conflict you make worse yourself.

runes.name: Ansuz
runes.hist: The Icelandic poem says óss (the Æsir), the Old English ós.
runes.up: Words, advice, insight from someone wiser.
runes.rev: Misunderstandings, bad advice, not being heard.

runes.name: Raidho
runes.hist: Old Norse reið, Old English rád.
runes.up: Travel, movement, the right rhythm.
runes.rev: Delay, wrong direction, a trip that should be postponed.

runes.name: Kaunan
runes.hist: The Icelandic poem says kaun (sore), the Old English cén (torch).
runes.up: Light in the dark, knowledge, a creative spark.
runes.rev: Something that aches, an insight you avoid.

runes.name: Gebo
runes.hist: Found only in the Old English rune poem (gyfu), not in the Younger Futhark.
runes.up: Gift, reciprocity, good cooperation.

runes.name: Wunjo
runes.hist: Found only in the Old English rune poem (wynn).
runes.up: Joy, fellowship, things falling into place.
runes.rev: Discontent, isolation, joy that fails to appear.

runes.name: Hagalaz
runes.hist: Old Norse hagall, Old English hægl.
runes.up: Disruption from outside that cleanses, a storm that passes.

runes.name: Naudiz
runes.hist: Old Norse nauð, Old English nýd.
runes.up: Need, limitation, patience under pressure.

runes.name: Isaz
runes.hist: Old Norse íss, Old English ís.
runes.up: Standstill, a pause, clarity when everything freezes.

runes.name: Jera
runes.hist: The Icelandic poem says ár (good year), the Old English gér.
runes.up: Harvest, results that come in their own time.

runes.name: Eihwaz
runes.hist: Found only in the Old English rune poem (eoh). Both the name and the sound value are disputed.
runes.up: Endurance, a link between the old and the new.

runes.name: Perthro
runes.hist: Old English peorð. No source says with certainty what the name means.
runes.up: The unknown, chance, something hidden coming to light.
runes.rev: Secrets that weigh on you, coincidences that go against you.

runes.name: Algiz
runes.hist: The original name is unknown; only a corrupted Old English form (eolhx) has survived. The rune was used by the SS as the “Lebensrune”.
runes.up: Protection, vigilance, setting boundaries.

runes.name: Sowilo
runes.hist: Old Norse sól, Old English sigel. A double sowilo was used as the SS sign.
runes.up: Sun, power, success, clarity.

runes.name: Tiwaz
runes.hist: Old Norse týr; the Icelandic poem calls him the one-handed god.
runes.up: Justice, courage, sacrificing something for what is right.
runes.rev: Injustice, discouragement, a fight that is not yours.

runes.name: Berkanan
runes.hist: Old Norse bjarkan, Old English beorc.
runes.up: Growth, new beginnings, care.

runes.name: Ehwaz
runes.hist: Found only in the Old English rune poem (eh).
runes.up: Cooperation, trust, moving forward.
runes.rev: Mistrust, restlessness, a partnership out of balance.

runes.name: Mannaz
runes.hist: Old Norse maðr, Old English mann.
runes.up: Yourself among others, community, self-knowledge.

runes.name: Laguz
runes.hist: Old Norse lögr, Old English lagu (sea).
runes.up: Intuition, flow, feelings.

runes.name: Ingwaz
runes.hist: Found only in the Old English rune poem (ing).
runes.up: Completion, inner growth, rest before something new.

runes.name: Dagaz
runes.hist: Found only in the Old English rune poem (dæg).
runes.up: Breakthrough, dawn, a new phase.

runes.name: Othala
runes.hist: Found only in the Old English rune poem (éþel, estate). The rune was used in SS badges and is used by extremists today.
runes.up: Home, inheritance, roots, what lasts.
runes.rev: Dispute over inheritance, rootlessness, old patterns that bind.
